summary.text: Mark Speed is the Democratic candidate for the North Carolina House of Representatives, District 7, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where he faces Republican Cory Thornton.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he has served on the Franklin County Board of Commissioners since 2017 and is a cattle and timber farmer and business owner.

paragraphs.text: Speed earned a high school diploma from Louisburg High School and an associate degree from Louisburg Community College.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, he said he is a lifelong Franklin County resident with 25 years in the hospitality industry as a mobile DJ, and that he volunteers with the fire department, the police department and Relay for Life.

In a 2022 survey, Speed's responses said he had been a Franklin County commissioner since his appointment in 2017 and that his father, James D. Speed, had represented the community in the North Carolina General Assembly for over 30 years.
Speed was the Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 11 in 2022, when incumbent Republican Lisa Barnes defeated him.
In 2026 he said he supports public education and opposes the rapid expansion of data centers, and that road infrastructure in the district is not being expanded to match growth.
He listed the AFL-CIO and Down Home NC as endorsers.
